question.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2x \\ x-3y\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as $\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

First, let's find the image of ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2}$ under $T,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2}) & =T([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & -2 & -5\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -7\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 \\ -4 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$
